excerpt: Scrape Anything is Context.dev's web-scraping endpoint: give it a URL and get clean Markdown, HTML, screenshots or structured data in one API call. Credits, pricing and alternatives.
content:
Scrape Anything is a web-scraping endpoint from Context.dev, an API company that supplies web data to software and AI agents. You send a URL and choose the outputs you want, such as HTML, Markdown, screenshots, images or raw bytes, and Context.dev handles the browser rendering, anti-bot blocks, proxies and retries. Each output comes back in its own field from a single call, and all of them share one base charge. You can also extract data as JSON against your own schema, run browser actions and read PDFs with OCR.

It sits inside a wider API that uses the same key and credits: mapping and crawling sites (up to 500 pages per call), web and news search, AI answers, brand data such as logos and colours, people enrichment and website monitors with webhooks. There are official SDKs for TypeScript, Python, Ruby, Go and PHP, a CLI and an MCP server for AI agents. The service is hosted only.

Scrape Anything launched on Product Hunt on 12 October 2026, Context.dev's fourth launch there, and finished #9 for the day with 104 upvotes. Product Hunt lists Yahia Bakour and Nikhil Radosevich among the team.

We have not tested Context.dev ourselves. This page brings together its official site, pricing page and documentation, its Product Hunt page and the official pricing pages of comparable APIs, and says where each fact comes from. If you scrape other sites, their terms and robots rules still apply to you.

use_cases: Feeding web pages to an AI agent or RAG pipeline as clean Markdown
Taking screenshots and HTML of a page in the same request
Extracting structured JSON from product or listing pages against your own schema
Crawling a documentation site into Markdown
Monitoring pages for changes and receiving webhooks

fit: build AI agents or data pipelines that need live web content
would rather not run your own headless browsers and proxies
want scraping, search and brand data under one API key and one credit balance
not_fit: must self-host your scraping (Context.dev is hosted only)
need a one-off data pull without a subscription: the pricing page says one-time lookups aren't supported
need LinkedIn data: a commenter asked and we found no answer on the launch page

pricing.intro: Context.dev sells monthly credit plans in US dollars. A basic scrape costs 1 credit, with JavaScript rendering, anti-bot handling and proxies included. Paying yearly gives two months free.

plans.name: Free
plans.detail: 1,000 credits a month, 1 concurrent request, 10 monitors, no card

plans.name: Developer
plans.detail: 7,500 credits a month, 10 concurrent requests; overage $2.20 per 1,000 credits

plans.name: Pro
plans.detail: 125,000 credits a month, 100 concurrent; overage $1.80 per 1,000; Slack support and spend controls

plans.name: Growth
plans.detail: 500,000 credits a month, 250 concurrent; overage $1.40 per 1,000; priority support

plans.name: Scale
plans.detail: 1,000,000 credits a month, 500 concurrent; overage $1.00 per 1,000; SSO/SAML

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.detail: 2,000,000+ credits, SCIM, 99.9% uptime SLA, annual invoicing, MSA and DPA

notes: Credit costs: a scrape from 1 credit (2 with browser actions); JSON extraction adds 4; PDF OCR adds 1 per page; crawling 1 per page; AI answers 10 or 100; brand data 10; people enrichment 20 per match.
Most failed requests aren't billed, but 404 pages are charged the base price.
Eligible startups and nonprofits get 30% off an annual plan for 12 months.
Refund terms are not stated on the pricing page.

alternatives.intro: From Product Hunt's alternatives list plus ScrapingBee. Prices come from each product's own pricing page, checked on 14 October 2026. Review scores are Product Hunt users' own.

items.name: Firecrawl
items.what: Web scraping and crawling API that returns LLM-ready Markdown and JSON
items.difference: The closest like-for-like option. Firecrawl charges for 403 and 404 error pages; Context.dev adds brand, people and news APIs under the same credits.

items.name: Apify
items.what: Platform of ready-made scrapers plus hosting for your own
items.starts_at: Free ($5 of usage a month); Starter $19/month
items.difference: Bills by compute units and offers a marketplace of site-specific scrapers rather than one unified endpoint.

items.name: ScrapingBee
items.what: Scraping API that handles headless browsers and proxies
items.starts_at: Hobby $19/month for 75,000 credits; 1,000 free trial credits
items.difference: No permanent free plan, only trial credits, and its pricing page doesn't show the credit multipliers for JavaScript or premium proxies.

alternatives.more: Product Hunt also lists Databar.ai, Browser Use and Browserbase.

liked: Getting Markdown for reading and structured data for the next step from the same API
asked: Whether it works with LinkedIn, and whether it offers residential proxies and authentication
What the rate limits are (the pricing page lists concurrency per plan, from 1 to 500 requests)

quotes.text: Markdown for reading and structured data for the next step, through the same API, makes sense.
quotes.author: Oleksii Sekundant

quotes.text: Does it work with LinkedIn? Do you offer residential proxies and authentication?
quotes.author: Ilyas

pros: Free plan with 1,000 credits a month and no card
JavaScript rendering, anti-bot handling and proxies included in the base price
Several output formats from one call for one charge
Scraping, crawling, search, brand data and monitors under one key
SDKs in five languages plus an MCP server
Versioned API with at least 90 days' notice for breaking changes
cons: Hosted only, with no self-hosted option
No one-off purchases; you need a plan
Launch questions about LinkedIn, proxies and authentication went unanswered on the page

x.none: We found no independent posts about Scrape Anything on X to link yet.

faq.a: There is a free plan with 1,000 credits a month, one concurrent request and no card. Paid plans start at $19 a month for 7,500 credits.

faq.q: How much does one scrape cost?
faq.a: From 1 credit, including JavaScript rendering, anti-bot handling and proxies. Browser actions make it 2 credits, and JSON extraction adds 4.
Context.dev limits concurrency by plan: 1 request at a time on Free, 10 on Developer, 100 on Pro, 250 on Growth and 500 on Scale.

faq.q: Am I charged for failed requests?
faq.a: Mostly not, according to the pricing FAQ. A 404 page is billed at the base price.

faq.q: Which languages and tools does it support?
faq.a: A REST API, official SDKs for TypeScript, Python, Ruby, Go and PHP, a CLI and an MCP server for AI agents.
Yes. Eligible startups and nonprofits get 30% off an annual paid plan for 12 months.
